sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa dell'aumento del VIX (+1.65%) e della debolezza delle borse europee (-0.33% STOXX 600). Il prezzo del petrolio è in aumento (+2.42% BRENT), il che potrebbe indicare una maggiore inflazione. Inoltre, le sanzioni contro l'Iran e le tensioni geopolitiche contribuiscono a un clima di incertezza.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the increase in VIX (+1.65%) and weakness in European stocks (-0.33% STOXX 600). Rising oil prices (+2.42% BRENT) may indicate higher inflation. Additionally, sanctions against Iran and geopolitical tensions contribute to uncertainty.

market_impact_summary.it: I mercati azionari europei sono deboli (-0.33% STOXX 600), mentre il VIX è in aumento (+1.65%). Il prezzo del petrolio è in spike (+2.42% BRENT), il che potrebbe avere un impatto negativo sull'inflazione e sulla crescita economica. Le borse asiatiche hanno chiuso in mixed, con il Nikkei in aumento (+2.50%) e l'Hang Seng in calo (-1.56%).
market_impact_summary.en: European stock markets are weak (-0.33% STOXX 600), while VIX is rising (+1.65%). Oil prices are spiking (+2.42% BRENT), which could negatively impact inflation and economic growth. Asian markets closed mixed, with Nikkei up (+2.50%) and Hang Seng down (-1.56%).

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.5%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.2%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

nella seduta precedente, l'S&P 500 ha registrato un aumento dello 0.13%, il VIX è salito dell'1.65%, segnale di maggiore avversione al rischio. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0.11%, a 99.33 L'oro è stabile a 4489 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio Brent è in rialzo del 2.42%, a 98.32 dollari. Il rendimento del decennale USA è in calo dello 0.45%, al 4.45%. Il BTP 10Y italiano è stabile, intorno al 3.73%.

Il presidente della Fed, Warsh, intende rivedere i segnali della banca centrale a Wall Street. Inoltre, gli Stati Uniti stanno valutando nuove tariffe su 60 economie, compresa la Cina, per questioni di lavoro forzato.

Oggi, saranno pubblicati i dati sull'inflazione CPI dell'Eurozona e sulla disoccupazione dell'UE. Nessuna dichiarazione recente delle banche centrali.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin scende del 3,37% a sessantasettemila centosessantacinque dollari. I flussi ETF mostrano una outflow di 483,8 milioni di dollari. Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti sanzioni del Tesoro USA contro gli scambi di criptovalute iraniani, che potrebbero aver aumentato l'incertezza nel mercato. 
  Tra le altcoin, Ethereum perde il 4,72% a milleottocentoottantatre dollari, Solana cede il 5,15% a settantacinque dollari e sedici centesimi, mentre BNB scende del 5,19% a seicentoquarantadue dollari e ventiquattro centesimi. 
  Il Fear & Greed Index è a 11, in zona di Extreme Fear, il che suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Outlook breve: oggi attenzione ai dati EU CPI Eurozona e disoccupazione EU. 
  Per approfondire, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. 
  Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 2.5%, Shanghai up 0.2%. This suggests a positive opening for European markets. In the previous session, the S&P 500 rose 0.13%, the VIX climbed 1.65%, a sign of increased risk aversion. The Dollar Index is up 0.11%, at 99.33 Gold is stable at $4,489 per ounce. Brent crude oil is up 2.42%, at $98.32 The 10-year US yield is down 0.45%, to 4.45%. The Italian 10Y BTP is stable, around 3.73%. The Fed's Warsh intends to review the central bank's signals to Wall Street. Additionally, the US is considering new tariffs on 60 economies, including China, over forced labor issues. Today, the Eurozone CPI inflation data and EU unemployment will be released. No recent statements from central banks. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin drops 3.37% to $67,165 ETF flows show an outflow of $483.8 million. This movement could be influenced by the recent US Treasury sanctions against Iranian crypto exchanges, which may have increased market uncertainty. Among altcoins, Ethereum loses 4.72% to $1,883, Solana falls 5.15% to $75.16, while BNB declines 5.19% to $642.24 The Fear & Greed Index is at 11, in Extreme Fear territory, suggesting investor caution. Short-term outlook: today, focus on EU CPI Eurozone and EU unemployment data. For more details, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Global pension asset allocations and debt markets
articles.snippet: The pensions sector is an important investor group in global financial markets and a key holder of government and corporate debt. This paper examines the evolution of pension fund asset allocations around the globe and documents important structural changes. Over time, pension investors have shifted from fixed income securities to mutual fund shares. In the meantime, they have also reallocated from traditional investments into alternative investments. Evidence from US pensions suggests that the decline in the fixed income share is due to both private and public debt. We hypothesise that a global decline in interest rates is one potential driver of this change. Using a global sample, we document that declining local currency government bond yields are associated with lower bond shares in pe

articles.title: The Rain in Spain Falls Harder on Ukraine: Rethinking the Spanish Civil War Analogy
articles.snippet: In 2023, the NATO Baltic Defense College in Tartu, Estonia devoted its entire annual conference to the Interwar Period (1919 to 1939), a theme repeated at subsequent conferences sponsored by national militaries and academic societies throughout the United States and Europe. Western scholars and foreign policy analysts, provoked by Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, seem persuaded that we are living at the close of another interwar era — one in which an egotistical European power shatters a decades-long continental truce, established and upheld by an international rules-based order, by invading a smaller neighbor ostensibly to defend threatened national minorities. articles.title: Ukraine's fiscal and financial challenges
articles.snippet: As it faces the exigencies of an existential war, Ukraine is confronted with stark fiscal and financial policy trade-offs, despite the mitigation provided by large-scale external financial support. So far, its authorities have kept monetary and financial stability under control beyond a relatively brief initial episode of turmoil in 2022. What is the broad fiscal equation for Ukraine looking forward, taking into account uncertainties about European funding beyond 2027? Can domestic revenue be raised? articles.title: The Toll Booth at the Throat of World Trade
articles.snippet: In late February 2026, Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz to foreign shipping. What began as a chaotic wartime closure has, in the past few days, hardened into something more consequential: an official sovereign toll regime, codified in Iranian law, and priced in cryptocurrency.On May 18, Iran operationally launched the Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a formal state bureaucracy with its own internet domain (pgsa.ir), account on X, and contact email. Since then, Tehran has delineated a “management supervision area” across the strait and announced a transit-permit scheme that converts Hormuz from an international waterway into a vetted toll plaza.Under the The post The Toll Booth at the Throat of World Trade appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: How Long Can Demand Destruction Keep a Lid on Oil Prices?
articles.snippet: In a somewhat puzzling market development, oil prices haven't spiked yet to record highs amid the worst supply disruption in history. That's because the market still hopes for a quick resolution to the Strait of Hormuz crisis (for more than three months now), global inventories have offered a supply buffer, the world's top crude importer, China, is staying away from spot purchases, and last but not least, demand destruction is accelerating amid the high prices. Beyond the near-term supply chaos and conflicting signals about the Middle East war,…
